cases.description: Emphasis nested 256 levels deep in a paragraph, each `*` a run of its own, is within the limit on inline nesting, and reads (§5.4, decision Y1).

A link inside 255 levels of emphasis is the 256th level, and reads (§5.4, decision Y1).

cases.description: A link inside 256 levels of emphasis is the 257th level, since links are inline levels too, and is a syntax error at the root (§5.4, decision Y1).
A heading holding 4,096 runs of `*` is within the run limit, and reads (§5.4, decision Y2).
A heading holding 4,097 runs is a syntax error at the root: runs in headings count toward the limit, as in a paragraph (§5.4, decision Y2).
A JSON section's $title holding 4,096 runs is within the run limit, and reads (§5.4, decision Y2).
A JSON section's $title holding 4,097 runs is a syntax error at the root: a data $title is read as a heading's inline content (§5.5), and its runs count toward the limit (§5.4, decision Y2).

An HTML block of only comments does not count as the first block, so an unknown data marker after it stands as the first block of a record without a title heading, and is feature-unsupported (§5.3, decisions Y3 and P6).
Likewise a yaml data block after an HTML block of only comments is the first block of a record without a title heading, and data-block-misplaced at the root (§5.3, decision Y3).
An HTML block that holds more than comments is the first block, so a yaml data block after it is a prose fence, and the record reads (§5.3, decision Y3).

Likewise an unknown data marker after an HTML block that holds more than comments is a prose fence, not the first block of a record without a title heading, and the record reads (§5.3, decisions Y3 and P6).

An HTML block that holds a comment and other text on one line holds more than comments, so it is the first block, a yaml data block after it is a prose fence, and the record reads (§5.3, decision Y3).
A JSON section's $title with emphasis nested 256 levels deep is within the limit on inline nesting, and reads (§5.4, decision Y1).

cases.description: One more level, 257, in a JSON section's $title is a syntax error at the root: a data $title is read as a heading's inline content (§5.5), and inline nesting counts toward the 256-level limit within it (§5.4, decision Y1).

A JSON section's $title is read with the link reference definitions of the record's $body values in scope, so the * in the label of a defined reference are no runs, as in Markdown, and 2,049 references with 2 of them each are within the run limit (§5.4, §5.5, decision Y2).
A reference link that a definition in the record's $body makes, inside 255 levels of emphasis in a JSON section's $title, is the 256th level, and reads (§5.4, §5.5, decision Y1).

cases.description: The same reference link inside 256 levels of emphasis is the 257th level, since reference links are inline levels too, and is a syntax error at the root, as in Markdown (§5.4, §5.5, decision Y1).
Two $titles beyond the nesting limit in one record give one syntax error at the root, as a Markdown record beyond a resource limit does (§5.4, Appendix D).
